item.text:
Use the map
\[
\phi:G\to G\cdot x,\qquad g\mapsto g\cdot x.
\]
Its fibers are precisely the left cosets of the stabilizer \(G_x\): two elements \(g,h\) send \(x\) to the same point exactly when \(h^{-1}g\in G_x\). Thus the orbit can be identified with the coset space \(G/G_x\).

Organize the proof by establishing:

1. \(\phi\) is surjective onto the orbit.
2. Every fiber has cardinality \(|G_x|\).
3. The finite set \(G\) is partitioned into \(|G\cdot x|\) such fibers.

Counting this partition gives the desired product formula. Finiteness is essential for interpreting these cardinalities via ordinary multiplication.
